To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) NUCB2 expression is downregulated in gastric cancer; (2) the protein is phosphorylated and undergoes post-translational modifications; (3) NUCB is expressed in the functioning gastric gland cells and lost in tumour cells; (4) NUCB may be implicated in the regulation of gastric secretion by establishing a releasable Ca2+-store in the ER/Golgi and/or mediating exocytosis.
NUCB 2 is expressed in the stomach and is downregulated in gastric cancer and that NUCB1 and NUCB2 have different expression patterns and functions in the stomach.
NUCB1 is expressed in the functioning gastric gland, is downregulated in gastric cancer and may be implicated in calcium homeostasis in the stomach.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the immunogenicity of NUCB1/2 and their physiological functions in the stomach, thereby contributing to the knowledge of these intriguing proteins.
the identification of a novel tumour antigen NUCB 2, its molecular characterisation in the gastric epithelium and the elucidation of its physiological functions.
the molecular mechanisms of the immune response against the tumour-associated antigen NUCB1/nesfatin and its physiological functions in the stomach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NUCB 2 is a novel tumour antigen with potential immunotherapeutic and prognostic implications.

the expression of NUCB1 is regulated in gastric tumours at the level of transcription, translation and post-translational modifications, and that the resulting NUCB2 protein isoform is a potential target of the immune response in gastric cancer patients.
NUCB is a novel tumour antigen that is down-regulated in gastric cancer and that its expression is associated with the physiological functions in the gastric epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NUCB is a novel tumour antigen with a potential role in gastric cancer and that it is expressed and regulated differently between the normal and tumour stomach.
NUCB is a novel tumour antigen in gastric cancer and that its expression is downregulated in gastric cancer.
NUCB 2 may be involved in various processes like calcium homeostatasis, TNF receptor shedding, hypothalamic control of feeding, gastric secretion and tumourigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NUCB1 and NUCB2 are two closely related EF-hand Ca2+-binding proteins that share a similar expression profile, are both expressed in the stomach and are implicated in gastric secretion.
NUCB is expressed in the stomach in a cell type-specific manner and is downregulated in gastric cancer, thus suggesting its potential as a biomarker for gastric cancer.
NUCB is a novel marker for the functioning parietal and chief cells and its loss in the tumour cells might be a consequence of the loss of the functioning gastric glands.
